the inhibition of IMPDH by mycophenic acid and tiazafurin causes differentiation in CEM leukemia cells.
the IMPDH inhibitors MPA and TZ can induce differentiation in human T- and B-lymphoblastic leukemia cells and that this differentiation is associated with a decrease of cellular IMPDH activity.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
IMPDH inhibitors are not the sole agents that induce the differentiation of CEM- cells.
IMPDH inhibitors induce cell differentiation in T- and B-lymphoid leukemia cells and that the differentiation process is associated with a decrease in cellular IMP dehydrogenases.

IMPDH inhibitors do not induce differentiation per se but rather that they induce the differentiation of cells which are already committed to differentiate, and this differentiation is not necessarily dependent upon the level of IMPDH activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the IMPDH inhibitors MPA and TZ are capable of inducing a T-cell suppressor/cytolytic phenotype in CEM2 cells.

IMPDH inhibitors are useful tools in the study of cell differentiation, and that the induction of differentiation in CEM cells by these compounds may provide an approach for circumventing the differentiation block of some tumor cells.
the inhibition of IMPDH by MPA or TZ induces differentiation in CEM cells, and that this differentiation is associated with the induction of a suppressor T-cell phenotype.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the IMPDH inhibitors MPA and TZ can induce a suppressor/cytoxic T-cell phenotype and differentiation in human T-cell leukemia CEM-2 cell line.

IMPDH inhibitors may have potential as inducers of cell differentiation in some tumor cell types, and this potential may be enhanced by the coadministration of purine nucleoside analogs that can bypass the IMPDH inhibition.
the differentiation induced by MPA and TZ in CEM- 2 cells is not a consequence of the decreased IMPDH activity and the altered IMPDH expression.
